observation: Intended pressurized sideways fan spray is not visible; effect reads more like an indistinct bright mass/vertical stream with no clear wall-impact sheeting, pooling, or dripping over lip.
expected_behavior: A sideways, pressurized fan-shaped jet from a pipe fitting that impacts the cabinet wall, breaks into a thin sheet running down, forms a pool on the cabinet floor, and begins dripping over the front lip.
actual_behavior: No readable fan spray or impact sheet; water detail largely unreadable (also compounded by severe overexposure), with only a vague vertical stream/droplets and no clear pooling/drip behavior.

suspected_parameters.fset.velocity_normal: too low or misdirected for a lateral fan; increase and ensure emitter normals face sideways
suspected_parameters.dset.timesteps_max: may be too low causing unstable/overly smeared motion
suspected_parameters.collisions: collider setup/padding may be preventing proper wall adhesion/sheeting

recommended_fix: First fix exposure so the motion can be evaluated (reduce world/background strength and correct water shader). Then to obtain a sideways fan spray and impact sheet: ensure inflow emitter normals point sideways toward the cabinet wall, keep fset.use_initial_velocity=True, increase fset.velocity_normal (e.g., 12-18), increase dset.resolution_max (>=128), increase dset.timesteps_max (>=10) if unstable, and reduce dset.particle_radius (e.g., 0.6-0.9 relative units). Verify wall/floor colliders are correctly set so liquid adheres and sheets down.
analysis_notes: Current render is blown out, which masks spray shape. However, even in silhouette the fan is missing, suggesting emitter direction/shape plus insufficient resolution/substeps.
